entries.location: packages/contracts/src/GianoSmartWallet.sol#L299-L306 (GianoSmartWallet._call)
entries.reason: False positive. Sending value to a target the owner chooses is what a wallet does. Slither checks _call on its own and ignores the access control of its callers. Only three functions call _call. execute and executeBatch are onlyEntryPointOrOwner, so the caller must be the EntryPoint, an owner address or the account itself. executeWithoutChainIdValidation is onlyEntryPoint and calls only address(this) with value 0. The EntryPoint runs a user operation only when validateUserOp accepts an owner's signature over the userOp hash. That hash covers the call data, so the signer sets the target and the value. EntryPoint.delegateAndRevert can call the account as the EntryPoint without a signature, but it always reverts, so no value leaves.
entries.followUp: G22 (independent contract review). Slither's id is a SHA3-256 hash of the finding text, which includes the file and line of the call (src/GianoSmartWallet.sol#300). Any edit that moves that line, or a rename of the file or function, changes the id. A Slither upgrade that changes the text format also changes it. When the id changes, review the finding again before you update the entry.

entries.location: packages/contracts/src/GianoSmartWalletFactory.sol:14 (contract GianoSmartWalletFactory)
entries.reason: False positive. createAccount passes all of msg.value to Solady LibClone.createDeterministicERC1967. For a new account, create2 sends the value to the account. For an existing account, a call sends the value and reverts if it fails. Aderyn 0.6.8 counts only Solidity .call{value: ...}, transfer, send and sendValue as sends, so it misses both sends in LibClone's inline assembly. Aderyn skips constructors in this check, so createAccount alone triggers the finding. The factory has no receive or fallback, so a plain transfer to it reverts. The payable constructor receives no ether, because the deploy code calls CreateX deployCreate3 without value.
entries.followUp: G22 (independent contract review). Remove this entry if a later Aderyn version recognises sends in assembly. Review it if createAccount stops being payable or stops forwarding msg.value.

entries.location: packages/contracts/src/paymaster/GianoPaymaster.sol:50 (contract GianoPaymaster)
entries.reason: False positive. depositFor and addStake forward all of msg.value to the EntryPoint (depositTo{value: ...} and addStake{value: ...}), and receive() reverts with DirectTransferNotAllowed. The inherited upgradeToAndCall is also payable. Only an UPGRADER_ROLE holder can call it, through the proxy. With empty data it rejects any value. With data, the new implementation that the upgrader chooses handles the value. Aderyn 0.6.8 does not count a call with value to a named function, such as depositTo{value: ...}, as a send. The deposit leaves through withdrawTo (withdrawTenant and withdrawFees) and as gas the EntryPoint charges. The stake leaves through withdrawStake, after unlockStake and the unstake delay. A withdrawal sent to the paymaster itself reverts, because receive() reverts.
entries.followUp: G22 (independent contract review). Remove this entry if a later Aderyn version recognises calls with value to a named function.

entries.location: packages/contracts/src/GianoSmartWalletFactory.sol:81 (GianoSmartWalletFactory.initCodeHash)
entries.reason: False positive. Aderyn flags any public or external function whose name starts with init or _init, unless its call graph contains a require, a revert or an initializer modifier. It does not check whether the function changes state. initCodeHash() is a view function. It returns the init code hash of the account's ERC-1967 proxy and changes no state.
entries.followUp: G22 (independent contract review).

entries.location: packages/contracts/src/utils/ERC1271InputGenerator.sol:48 (ERC1271InputGenerator constructor)
entries.reason: By design. Aderyn flags every return in inline assembly. This one ends the constructor of a helper that is meant to run only inside an eth_call. The constructor returns the account's replay-safe hash, even before the account is deployed. No deploy script or release deploys the contract; only the Foundry tests create it. No code in this repo calls it today, because the wallet SDK computes the replay-safe hash off-chain.
entries.followUp: G22 (independent contract review). The helper fails when the hash starts with byte 0xEF (EIP-3541), about 1 in 256 hashes. Decide in G22 whether to fix or remove the contract.

entries.location: .gitleaks.toml (allowlist AF-008). The keys are used in the devnet compose files, e2e/devnet, tests, and the dev defaults of the bundler and the paymaster CLIs.
entries.reason: Public by design. These are the ten private keys Anvil derives from the public test mnemonic (test test test test test test test test test test test junk), and Foundry prints them every time Anvil starts. They fund accounts only on local devnets and in tests, and the code marks them as never legitimate outside a devnet. Each regex matches the whole secret, with or without 0x, so any other key still fails the scan.
entries.followUp: Renew while the devnet and the tests use the Anvil keys.

entries.location: .gitleaks.toml (allowlist AF-009). Today: devnet token addresses under defaultToken in deploy/docker-compose.infrastructure.yml, services/custom-example/.env.development, e2e/tests/demo/demo-erc20.spec.ts and the spa-parity fixtures.
entries.reason: False positive. gitleaks rule generic-api-key flags a value assigned to a key whose name contains token or key. These values are Ethereum addresses (0x and exactly 40 hex characters), which are public by design. A private key has 64 hex characters, so it does not match and still fails the scan. A real secret with the exact shape of an address is unlikely.
entries.followUp: Renew while configs hold contract addresses under such key names.

entries.location: .gitleaks.toml (allowlist AF-010). Today: the Sepolia RPC URL in forge-std's src/StdChains.sol, copied into packages/contracts/releases/v1, v2 and v3/standard-input.json.
entries.reason: Public by design. forge-std ships this Infura project ID in its default chain list, so every Foundry project that builds with forge-std holds it. It is not our key, and it gives access to nothing of ours. The release standard-input.json files embed the forge-std source, so each new release adds the key again. The regex matches only this exact key, so any other Infura key still fails giano-infura-key.
entries.followUp: Renew while forge-std ships this key. Remove the entry when a forge-std update drops it and no release file holds it.

entries.location: giano-wallet-byo, both arches: the esbuild 0.25.4 binary (repo/node_modules/.pnpm/@esbuild+linux-*@0.25.4), Go 1.23.8. Fixed in Go 1.24.12, 1.25.6.
entries.reason: No fix in this image yet. The vulnerability is in the Go standard library (Go 1.23.8) compiled into the esbuild 0.25.4 binary. serve.mjs runs esbuild at container start to bundle the image's own SPA source, and tsdown, tsx and vite also install esbuild 0.25.4 in this image, so upgrading the e2e workspace's esbuild does not remove it. Newer esbuild releases are built with Go 1.26.5, which still has some of these vulnerabilities, and Trivy cannot read their Go version, so an upgrade would hide findings rather than fix them. The vulnerable code is Go's network, TLS, certificate, URL, mail, MIME, XML and HTML template handling, and os.Root, which Go 1.23 does not have. esbuild's input here is only the image's own source files: it takes no input from users or the network. giano-wallet-byo is the BYO test origin: it runs in dev and e2e only, never in a real deployment.
entries.followUp: Rebuild giano-wallet-byo so it ships only the esbuild that serve.mjs uses, on a release built with a fixed Go version, then remove AF-011 to AF-036.

entries.location: giano-devnet, both arches: apt 2.4.14 in the Foundry v1.7.1 base (Ubuntu 22.04). Fixed in 2.4.15ubuntu0.1.
entries.reason: No fix in this image yet. The vulnerable package is part of the Ubuntu 22.04 layer of the Foundry v1.7.1 base image (ghcr.io/foundry-rs/foundry, pinned by digest), and Foundry has not rebuilt that image. A newer Foundry release would also change the Foundry that determinism.yml uses to build the contracts, so it needs its own change. giano-devnet is the ABIP-2 exception image (#165): its entrypoint is anvil, it has no RUN step, and it serves a local chain to local and CI clients only. It is never deployed.
entries.followUp: Upgrade Foundry, together with determinism.yml, to a release whose image has the fixed packages, or move giano-devnet to a hardened base (#165). Then remove AF-037 to AF-043.
